framework_rationale: The board holds a diagnosis (competitor price) and a proposal (30 AEs) that the data contradicts; Situation-Complication-Resolution lets us test the plan in force before offering the alternative, problem first.

candidates.text: The slowdown is a retention failure, not a sales failure: fix onboarding now (€0.8M) and release AE hiring only when first-year churn recovers.
Approve the 30 AEs but cut the 2026 new-ARR expectation to the ramp-adjusted figure.
Growth slowed because churn rose; the company should invest in customer success.

governing_thought: ARR growth fell to 9.2% because rising churn and weaker expansion cut net new ARR by €5.6M while new sales held; the 2026 budget should first reverse the €0.8M onboarding cut, which lost about €2.5M of ARR, and release the €3.6M AE hire only once first-year churn recovers.

key_line.message: Net new ARR fell by €5.6M because churn rose by €4.5M and expansion fell by €1.3M; new sales held, win rate stayed between 23% and 24%.
First-year churn more than doubled from 12% to 26% after the onboarding team was cut from 14 to 6; the €0.8M saving cost about €2.5M of ARR.
The 30-AE plan books €9M that the 9-month ramp cannot deliver in 2026 (about €5.6M) and feeds new customers into an onboarding that loses 26% of them.
Restore onboarding now and release AE hiring at a retention gate: retention levers worth up to €3.8M, with the €1.8M gap closed by gated AE hiring.

target.statement: Working target (inferred, no target given): recover the €5.6M fall in net new ARR, back to the 2024 level of €10.4M

levers.statement: Restore the onboarding team (6 back to 14) and bring first-year churn from 26% back to the 2024 rate of 12%
levers.validate: Time to first value and 90-day activation of the Q1-Q2 2026 cohorts; first-year churn tracking toward 12% by end Q2 2026

levers.statement: Recover expansion ARR to the 2024 level (€4.3M) through implemented, active customers
levers.validate: Account-level analysis of 2025 expansion versus implementation status (tests H4) before booking it in the plan, Q1 2026

gap.how_closed: Not closed by retention alone. Closed by the AE hiring released at the gate (run-rate €300k per productive AE); ARR from a mid-year release lands mostly in 2027, so the board should expect net new ARR below the 2024 level in 2026 if the gate is not met.

current_plan.statement: CRO plan: hire 30 account executives in Q1 2026 at €3.6M a year, adding €9M of new ARR in 2026

cost_if_kept.note: €3.6M a year committed against a diagnosis the data rejects; 2026 new ARR overstated by about €3.4M; churn leak on new customers unaddressed

options.statement: CRO plan as proposed: 30 AEs in Q1 2026, onboarding stays at 6 people
options.note: Excess churn charged at the 2025 cohort size; with more new customers into an unchanged 6-person team the exposure is larger (lower bound).

options.statement: Retention first: restore onboarding to 14 now; pre-approve the 30-AE envelope, released in tranches once the retention gate is met (earliest mid-2026)
options.note: AE opex is 0 until the gate, then up to €3.6M a year pro rata; no AE ARR is booked in the 2026 budget, so there is no promise to fall short of. Excess churn 0 only if the fix works (to be validated at the gate); a partial fix leaves a residual that applies equally to O3. Trade-off: delaying the AE hire gives up part of the 2026 AE contribution.

options.statement: Do both now: restore onboarding to 14 and hire 30 AEs in Q1 2026
options.note: Excess churn 0 on the same 'if the fix works' basis as O2, but a 14-person team sized for 2024 volume would also onboard the extra AE-won customers: capacity risk not quantifiable from the sources. Commits €3.6M before the sales-capacity diagnosis is tested.

asks.statement: Approve restoring the onboarding team from 6 to 14 people (€0.8M a year) from January 2026
Reject the Q1 2026 hire of 30 AEs as proposed and remove the €9M AE-driven new ARR from the 2026 budget
Approve an AE envelope of up to €3.6M a year, released by the CFO in tranches when the retention gate is met
Commission an account-level expansion review (implementation status versus expansion) to validate the €1.3M expansion lever

gates.statement: Retention gate for releasing AE hiring
gates.criterion: Median time to first value of new customers back to 21 days or less and early churn of the 2026 cohorts on track for first-year churn of 12% or less
Ramp curve of AEs hired in 2024-2025 confirms productivity assumption A001 before the first tranche is hired

kpis.name: New ARR per AE versus ramp curve
